annotations.text:
THE WHOLE APP — CINEMA
Eleven screens, one system: warm ground, Instrument Serif over Archivo, art tiles with real depth, one filled control per screen, numbers always tabular.

The rule everywhere: ART AND NUMBERS FIRST, TEXT ON DEMAND. Nothing is deleted — every paragraph the old screens showed still exists, one click down, still reachable by find-in-page.

Row 1 is the path in: front door → the recorded search → the slate → the brief.

ROW 2 — MAKING AND RELEASING
Commissioning shows the work arriving rather than narrating the wait. Shows and Season lead with artwork and the release state; the season page also sells the SECOND product — everyone at the edge of it is a show of their own.

The season page was the worst screen in the old app: ~1,500 words closed, ~3,000 opened, a 12-name cast list duplicated from /cast, and the hidden_from explanation buried in a 62-word tooltip.

ROW 3 — THE PRODUCT CLAIM
This is the half the demo turns on, and the half that most needed the change: /cast was 17 rows × ~72 words, with the same two numbers printed as a sentence next to a bar already showing them.

Now: faces, and one bar each. The character page keeps knows/blind unfolded and at size. The spin-off page keeps the validator report unfolded AND shows the control pair — same character, same moment, written twice, only one allowed to pass. A claim behind a fold is a claim nobody read.

SPEC AND EARLIER PASSES
Row anatomy and the three legal states, where it started, and the directions set aside.

Sources: Stephen Few's bullet-graph spec (track intensities, no borders or ticks), FBref scouting reports (fixed slot order), the Linear teardown (one job for the accent), NN/g data tables (single-open accordion), Pencil & Paper (tabular numerals, right-aligned).
